Task: Predict aspect ratings for a restaurant review.

Aspects:
- food: taste, freshness, portion, menu quality
- service: staff attitude, speed, accuracy, helpfulness
- atmosphere: cleanliness, comfort, ambience, noise, decor

Rating scale:
1 = very negative, 2 = negative, 3 = neutral/mixed/unclear, 4 = positive, 5 = very positive

Rules:
- Output MUST contain exactly 3 pairs in this exact order: food, service, atmosphere.
- Output format MUST be exactly: <food, X>, <service, Y>, <atmosphere, Z>
- Use ONLY integers 1-5. No extra text. No explanations.
- If an aspect is not mentioned, infer from the overall sentiment; if truly unclear, use 3.

Review:
I am extremely disappointed with my recent experience. This was supposed to be my birthday dinner, and instead it turned out to be the worst one I’ve had. My girlfriend originally wanted to take me to Mama Sushi for a nice celebration, but after leaving the spa I decided I wanted Popeyes since I hadn’t had it in a while, and we could share it with her mom at home. I placed my order online for pickup. When I arrived, the cashier didn’t realize I had ordered 2 drinks—I had to remind him. While he got them, I checked my bag and saw I only had 1 small coleslaw instead of the large I ordered, and 3 small mashed potatoes instead of 1 large (which is NOT the same). When I got home and opened the chicken, it was old, possibly recooked, burnt, and completely dried out. I have pictures of everything—it was unacceptable. On top of that, my Popeyes signature sauce was missing. This location completely ruined what should have been an enjoyable birthday meal. I regret not going to Mama Sushi instead. I will never return to the Popeyes on Kennedy Blvd in North Bergen, and I’ll be sharing this review and the photos on my Instagram review page.

It would be nice to see some ecuadorian art on the walls perhaps from local artists. If you take a look at our photos you can see that it all looks delicious. Review:
UPDATE: Went back and tried the encebollado (fish stew or otherwise known as the national hangover soup), the salchicha seca (blood sausage), lunch special of caldo de bola (beef, plantain and peanut soup) accompanied by grilled chicken breast with rice and red beans. The encebollado in this case lacked flavor and onions and cilantro, possibly aji peruano. It tasted like a basic fish stew with yucca. It was loaded with fish, this is a plus. I took it home and added a fresh handful of cilantro and red onions and it was better. I would give it a 3.5, I have def had better! The blood sausage was delicious and the portion was huge, a bit pricey coming in at almost 20 bucks! I would give it 4 stars. Caldo de bola was delicious not to thick and not too much peanut sauce, could have used a bit more meat but overall I give it 4.5 stars. The grilled chicken was soo tender very well cooked and flavorful, rice was good and red beans though a tad salty again, delicious. For the lunch special of 15 bucks I would give it 4.5 stars. Service was decent this time, have several staff standing around and you have to catch their attention for assistance Overall I give them a 4.5, place is a bit inconsistent with flavors and service, but worth trying for the first time and/or to open your possibility up to the Ecuadorian cuisine. Food was really good, but a bit salty, still edible so deserves the 5 stars. We arrived past 830pm and service was still great. Atmosphere is nice and suits the pricing of each plate. (more expensive than other Ecuadorian spots, but worth it). Tried the Desayuno Montubio (steak, peppers, onions tomato in red sauce, two eggs and a plantain cheese and pork meat/rind ball) , bolon was mixto with both sweet and regular plantain. The flavor was very different, more buttery, but very good! They did not skimp on chicharrón or cheese. The meat was tender, sauce a bit salty. Also had Seco de Gallina (Hen Stew, usually in a beer sauce). It was very good, great portion of meat, 3 big slices of sweet plantains, and a few slices of avocado. However, sauce again a bit salty. The hot sauce is amazing and the Naranjilla shake in water, was SPOT ON! For appetizer had the Maduro con Queso (sweet plantains with cheese) good portion, well cooked. It did not bring ecuadorian cheese, but available upon request. (also sell it by the pound) Def recommend trying this place out, and will def come back to try other plates

Review:
I wanted to like this place, but the experience left me feeling overcharged and misled. This is effectively counter service. You order at the bar, pick up your own food at the window, and clear your own space. Despite that, a mandatory 20 percent gratuity is automatically added, even on a quiet evening with no game playing. There were maybe 20 people in the entire place. The signage suggests the mandatory tip applies during games, yet it was applied regardless, with no explanation and no option. On top of that, the payment screens still prompt you to tip more, which feels excessive given that the service is entirely self directed. At that point it feels less like a gratuity and more like a surcharge. The food did not justify the pricing. I ordered the beef brisket, which arrived dry, overcooked, and served on plain white bread with no sauce. The fries were plentiful, but I did not come for fries. At nearly 27 dollars for the brisket alone, I expected something significantly better than average. To make matters worse, a pretzel listed at 14.99 was first charged correctly, then later rung up at 16.99, plus the mandatory 20 percent tip again. I did not feel like arguing over two dollars, but it reinforced the overall impression of sloppy pricing and a lack of transparency. By the end of the night, two beers, two basic meals, and a pretzel came close to 90 dollars, for counter service and mediocre food. I understand Newark pricing and I am not opposed to tipping when it is earned. What I object to is mandatory tipping layered on top of premium prices, especially when the customer is doing most of the work. There are better options nearby that offer clearer pricing, better food, and a more honest value proposition. I will not be returning.

However, after speaking w/quite a few people (most of whom had a similar experience w/OMG), I decided to share my experience w/full transparency. So let's get to it...my experience was downright HORRIBLE! Let me explain as best I can w/o being too lengthy (if that's possible). Ok, I am a foodie, and will travel anywhere for good food/service. My family also owned a restaurant so I totally understand what it takes to make a restaurant successful. W/that said, from the moment I walked in people were complaining about the wait. U could literally cut the tension in the air w/a knife. Now, I don't mind waiting because good food takes time...so I'm ok w/that. However, many of the people did not feel the same way. They may have ordered 1 or 2 small things and had to wait nearly an hour...so they were very upset. When I finally get to the register I asked if they had real or imitation crab meat. The young lady (who was great) said she did not know and to let her ask (which was the appropriate thing to do). A little guy w/dreads gave her attitude when she asked the question. So I then asked, and he replied that it was real crab meat. Now I am starting to get annoyed because the bad customer service reviews that I read prior to going are starting to show face. I finally place my order and go wait outside. While outside many of the people going in and out are complaining about either the wait or the service...I mean mostly everyone (no exaggeration). People who left and came back nearly an hour later still found that their food was not ready. One older lady ordered 2 items but they only gave her one and made her wait for the other. Why not have both ready at the same time? That didn't make sense! Anyhow, the elderly woman also mad because people who had come in and ordered way after she did, got their food first. She was not happy, to say the least. So I would go back and forth between the waiting area and outside so I could check on my food. One time doing so, the little guy w/the dreads was mumbling and no one knew what he was saying. He looked my way and I didn't respond because I had no clue what he was saying. So as I sit there staring at them, they continue to mumble things about me (I assume). Because I was not happy by any means. I was sitting w/a few ladies and they were appalled w/the service and behavior as well. One said she and her husband experienced the same thing a few days earlier, and the other lady said she'd never come back. When I finally got my food (after 40 plus minutes or so), I noticed that my container was very messy. They just throw U a bag to bag ur own food, and when some people told me to check how it looked....I was mortified. My food looked nothing like the pictures...i mean nowhere close. I was on 🔥! I will post pictures so u guys can see what i'm talking about. Also, when the guy brought my food up he said to the owner, this is his...which really disturbed me. If he was cooking, how did he know what I ordered? Did u purposely mess up my food or do something to it? And I'm not implying that he or anyone did. However, when have such poor customer service, people are cussing and acting inappropriately, it makes u think the worst. In closing, I want them to succeed but they have to do better. Review:
I went on a Tuesday night and had a very easy time finding parking. There is free parking behind the restaurant and street parking. The entrance is also from the back of the restaurant. Service was excellent. It felt like going to your friend's house and being helped by the kindest Korean mom. They don't have buttons at your table to request assistance but the staff is always walking around, incredibly attentive, and super warm and friendly. My entire group ordered the set and the food came out immediately. It being our first time, the server went over how to tackle the spread and explained the soups. The food was excellent! So many delicious veggie banchan and the set is basically a BYOB - build your own bibimbap. There were lots of banchan I've never had before like chopped chili pepper, shishito pepper, eggplant, and a white mushroom that looked like a shorter seafood mushroom. My favorites were the small patty sized kimchi pancakes, the acorn jelly salad (could use more acorn jelly 😬), and the entire BYOB experience... that's pretty much all the food 😆 the sea snail dish was good but I wasn't a huge fan of the texture. I eat pescatarian and it reminded me of bony cartilage. The best part is that you can get unlimited Barley rice and banchan. It was so much food that we never finished our first set. We ended up taking the leftovers home and it was enough for another meal. Overall, I would definitely go back and absolutely recommend it. There is an a la carte menu and I would love to try some of those dishes with a larger group.

I had an incredible dining experience at Oliveira’s! From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere was warm and inviting. The service was outstanding – the staff was attentive and friendly, making sure every detail of our meal was perfect. The star of the show, of course, was the meat. The variety of cuts offered on the traditional rodizio service was impressive, and each one was cooked to absolute perfection. The picanha was incredibly tender and flavorful, and the garlic steak was a standout. The meat was seasoned just right, and the constant flow of fresh cuts kept us coming back for more. The salad bar was also a pleasant surprise, offering a wide selection of fresh vegetables, cheeses, and traditional Brazilian sides like feijoada and pão de queijo. The caipirinhas were the perfect complement to the meal, and we couldn't resist ordering dessert – the passion fruit mousse was light and refreshing. Overall, this is hands down one of the best Brazilian steakhouses I've visited. The food, service, and ambiance all exceeded expectations, and I will definitely be returning soon! Highly recommend to anyone who loves great meat and a truly authentic experience.

2.5 stars. I have no idea why this place has as many good reviews as they do. We went here for the AYCE sushi but decided to go a la cart. I'm glad that we did because the rolls were just average. Nothing to write home about. They were busy on a Thurs night and we had to wait around 10 mins to get seated. There isn't much place to wait inside, so we stood outside. This isn't a big deal at night but if you come here during the day, it might be a wait in the heat. The ambiance is casual, sports bar with a few booths. We ordered the Call 911 roll, the Kiss of Fire, the Spicy salmon roll, the Takoyaki, the Unagi sushi and a Hot sake. We love spicy food so a lot of our decision-making was based on the number of spice stars next to the rolls. The Call 911, which had 5 spice stars next to it and was recommended by the server as their hottest, was nowhere close to being spicy. In fact, the Kiss of Fire, which had 3 stars, had more of a kick. The server ended up getting us some spicy Korean sauce to heat things up. The rolls overall were ok. Same thing with the spicy salmon roll. It was fine. Nothing to write home about. The Takoyaki and the Unagi were just disappointing. Unlike the usual Takoyaki, these were half balls instead of full balls. They also didn't have the bonito flakes and the octopus was more pureed than diced. The Unagi looked nicer than it tasted. Instead of tasting the rice and the eel as a combination, it amalgamated into one melted bite, which wasn't as fun. The sake was fine. All in all, this was a very average dining experience and we will look for alternatives when we come back to Vegas next time.
